headline: With the US 10 year at 5.12 percent and a December Fed increase about 75 percent priced, Tuesday gains in New York went to the Dow and small caps rather than technology, and India opens its largest ever IPO today, Jio Platforms at 30,213 crore rupees, after foreign investors pulled close to 50,000 crore rupees out this month.

summary.us: The Dow rose 1.02 percent to 52,495.88 and the Russell 2000 1.65 percent to 2,773.42 after 3M beat estimates and raised full year guidance, while the Nasdaq Composite ended flat at 26,424.82 and technology was the only sector to close lower; the S&P 500 added 0.28 percent to 7,712.57 and the VIX fell 6.13 percent to 17.31. The 10 year yield eased to 5.117 percent from about 5.31 percent earlier this month, General Motors fell about 7 percent despite beating estimates, and Meta and Tesla report after the US close tonight.
summary.india: Exchanges were shut on Tuesday for Dussehra, so the last close is Monday: the Nifty 50 fell 1.11 percent to 22,888.95 and the Sensex 1.17 percent to 73,852.90 as private banks and IT dragged, with Axis Bank down 4.19 percent after September quarter profit of 7,003 crore rupees missed the 7,124 crore rupee consensus compiled by LSEG. Foreign institutions sold about 1,149 crore rupees against 3,201 crore rupees of domestic buying, taking October foreign outflows to roughly 49,900 crore rupees, the rupee is at 94.77 a dollar, and the Jio Platforms and Paras Healthcare IPOs open today.
summary.global: China third quarter GDP of 4.5 percent beat the 4.4 percent consensus, but the Nikkei 225 fell 1.30 percent to 64,075.37 as SoftBank dropped about 6 percent with its five year credit default swaps at 432 basis points, the widest since November 2022. Europe closed slightly lower, with the Stoxx 600 at 638.64 and the DAX at 25,304.42 both down 0.1 percent and London banks the biggest drag, while crude swung on a reported United States and Iran peace proposal: Brent settled little changed at 109.64 dollars and the front month WTI quote dropped to 98.55 dollars as the November contract expired and the December contract took over, so most of that 4.9 percent fall is the contract roll rather than the market.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to the cost of money rather than the promise of AI. Hot September CPI and PPI prints pushed fed funds futures toward pricing another quarter point increase by year end, and with the 10 year above 5 percent the market stopped asking whether AI compute is wanted and started asking who funds it: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit a record, the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell for eight straight sessions, and the Nasdaq shed 4.48 percent on the week while the Dow, carried by defensives, held a 0.67 percent gain. India went the other way, with the Nifty adding 3.44 percent as IT earnings landed well and the rupee rallied for six sessions on RBI intervention, even as October foreign outflows neared 50,000 crore rupees. Commodities split sharply, with WTI up 7.83 percent on a large US inventory draw and Strait of Hormuz risk while silver dropped 5.83 percent and gold was little changed, and crypto drifted lower on continued spot ETF outflows and close to a billion dollars of leveraged liquidations. Next week brings the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms IPO, the largest in Indian history, alongside Tesla and Netflix earnings, Infosys on Friday and flash PMIs, all inside the Fed blackout that runs to the 28 October decision.
